title: Fynaptix · AI & Compute Research
heading: AI & Compute Intelligence
subheading: The capex supercycle, silicon stack, foundation-model giants & the bubble debate
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. AI is the market's most crowded trade; concentration and drawdown risk are significant. Verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.label: Amazon (~$220B), Alphabet ($195–205B), Microsoft (capex guide raised to ~$190B CY2026 from ~$175B / ~$255–260B FY2027 all-in), Meta ($130–145B after twice raising its floor) and Oracle (S&P models $90–95B FY2027) — combined $825–855B. The four hyperscalers ex-Oracle are pacing ~$725B for 2026 alone, up 77% from ~$410B in 2025. Debt funding still sits near 32% of capex over the trailing twelve months (FactSet)

kpis.sub: ANTHROPIC VS. OPENAI — LATEST PRIVATE VALUATIONS
kpis.label: Anthropic holds its $965B Series H mark, revenue run-rate near $65B annualized at end of July, targeting an ~Oct 26 IPO with a first-day market cap near $1.85T. OpenAI, still marked at $852B via its August employee tender, crossed $40B in annualized revenue (~$3.3B/month) in August but filed only a confidential S-1 (June 8) and isn't expected to list until 2027

Global venture funding per Crunchbase ($300B in Q1, $205B in Q2), already topping all of 2025's $440B; AI captured ~70–80% of it, dipping from ~80% in Q1 to the low-70s in Q2. OpenAI and Anthropic alone absorbed $217B — 43% of every venture dollar invested worldwide this year

kpis.sub: BROADCOM'S NEW FY2027 AI SEMICONDUCTOR OUTLOOK (RAISED SEPT 2)

bear_case.title: The revenue gap
bear_case.description: The industry has now committed an estimated $3–4T to AI infrastructure against an annualized return requirement of roughly $600–800B in new profit (up from Sequoia's original $200B framework in late 2023), while actual AI-attributable revenue runs an estimated $50–150B a year — a gap that keeps widening as the top-5 hyperscaler 2026/FY27 capex total climbs to $825–855B. For context, cloud computing's capex-to-revenue ratio at the same point in its adoption curve (2011) was roughly 2.4:1, far below today's multiple. The BIS's June 2026 annual report still names an AI-capex bust as one of its top three risks to global financial stability.

bear_case.title: Rates are the transmission mechanism — but strength can still win the argument
bear_case.description: The 30-year Treasury has held near 19-year highs (~5.25–5.29% through early September) as AI-linked debt issuance adds to bond-supply pressure, and stocks have chopped session to session on the news (S&P 500 +0.46% one day, -0.4% the next in the first week of September). But Broadcom's Sept 2 beat-and-raise and Dell/HPE's Sept 3 jump on AI-server demand kept the fundamental-demand side of the argument intact — a reminder the debate can swing hard in either direction week to week.

bear_case.title: Off-balance-sheet obligations turning concrete
bear_case.description: Moody's flags ~$662B of signed-but-not-commenced data-center lease commitments sitting off hyperscaler balance sheets, with debt funding of the buildout holding near 32% of capex over the trailing twelve months (FactSet). Oracle is now the starkest case: S&P downgraded its credit to BBB- on Aug 25 (one notch above junk), FY26 free cash flow already came in at -$23.7B, and S&P projects the deficit widening to ~$42B in FY27 even as the company insists it won't add more debt this calendar year — leaning on a $20B equity raise instead.

bear_case.title: Circular financing
bear_case.description: Nvidia's proposed OpenAI financing backstop remains capped under $120B and covers only the first phase of an Ohio data center — a sign the market's pushback on "vendor financing its own customers" is affecting deal structure. Michael Burry has escalated, calling Nvidia's revenue "majority circularly financed" and adding shorts on Oracle, Micron and Nebius plus March 2027 puts on the semiconductor ETF. Separately, analysts have tallied more than $800B in criss-crossing investment and purchase commitments across the broader AI supply chain, a pattern CNBC's Jim Cramer publicly compared to dot-com-era financing on July 27. Nvidia's own newly confirmed $12.93B Hugging Face acquisition (Sept 2) extends the web one layer further, from chips into the open-source model-hosting layer its customers depend on.

bear_case.title: Depreciation clock
bear_case.description: Hyperscalers depreciate AI hardware over 5–6 years; bears argue the real economic life is closer to 2–3 years, understating depreciation by an estimated ~$176B across 2026–2028 and flattering reported earnings (Oracle by an estimated 26.9%, Meta by 20.8%, by 2028 on this analysis). Michael Burry has doubled down on shorts in Oracle, Micron and Nebius, plus fresh March 2027 puts on the semiconductor ETF, calling current pricing "what the top of a boom looks like." Counterpoint: NVIDIA and CoreWeave point to secondary-market pricing and long-term contracts as evidence older silicon stays productive longer than the bear case assumes.

bear_case.title: Layoffs while capex soars
bear_case.description: Oracle's latest round of job cuts took effect with the Sept 1 start of its fiscal Q2 — on top of the ~21,000 already cut — even as S&P now models $90–95B of FY2027 capex funded substantially by a fresh equity raise. Microsoft cut roughly 4,800 more in July. Tech-sector layoffs remain near a 20-year high. The juxtaposition — record infrastructure spend, shrinking headcount, and disclosures like Meta's own AI systems breaching internal test environments — keeps fueling the argument that AI economics lean on cost-cutting elsewhere in the business, not on AI revenue itself.

bear_case.title: Concentration everywhere
bear_case.description: AI is simultaneously the market's largest index weight, VC's largest allocation (OpenAI and Anthropic alone took 43% of a record $510B global H1 2026 venture total), and this hub's connective thread — a drawdown would hit robotics, nuclear, storage and quantum sentiment at once. Commentary this week has flagged unusually high concentration among megacap AI names as a risk that could fuel an outsized drop if institutions start trimming winners. Counterpoint: infrastructure vendors keep posting record quarters (Broadcom's Sept 2 beat-and-raise, Dell/HPE's Sept 3 jump on AI-server demand) — some strategists call the bear case premature given actual demand signals.

catalysts.title: Nvidia confirms definitive $12.93B deal to acquire Hugging Face

catalysts.description: Both hardware makers rallied premarket after lifting guidance on AI server demand, broadening the "AI capex is real" signal beyond the chipmakers themselves.

positions.name: NVIDIA
positions.note: Confirmed the $12.93B Hugging Face acquisition (Sept 2, closing H1 2027) and CFO Kress guided to 70%+ FY2028 revenue growth with Jensen Huang calling demand 'much greater than 70%' — fundamentals keep improving, but trimming two points to fund Broadcom's and Microsoft's fresher, more concrete beats this week, and because a second straight acquisition adds real integration and regulatory-scrutiny risk on top of Michael Burry's escalating 'majority circularly financed' rhetoric. Also sits in this hub's Quantum, Robotics and AI Biotech sleeves — don't double-count sizing.

positions.name: TSMC
positions.note: Raised its own 2026 revenue growth outlook to 'slightly above 40%' and lifted 2026 capex to $60–64B — a second straight upward revision with the least circular-financing exposure of any name on this page. Taiwan geopolitical risk remains the single largest tail risk in the entire hub.

positions.name: Alphabet
positions.note: No new company-specific catalyst this edition — the $195–205B capex guide has now held steady for two straight editions, still the most disciplined hyperscaler on that metric. Trimming one point purely to make room for Broadcom's and Microsoft's more concrete news this week, not because the thesis weakened. Also appears in the Quantum sleeve — don't double-count.

positions.name: Microsoft
positions.note: Capex guide moved up to ~$190B for CY2026 (from ~$175B) on top of the still-unfulfilled $80B Azure order backlog — a real, disclosed increase in spending commitment this time, not just a lease-accounting reclassification. FY2027 all-in spend (with leased capacity) still points near $255–260B. Also in the Quantum sleeve — don't double-count.

positions.name: Amazon
positions.note: No fresh Amazon-specific catalyst this edition; last week's raise to ~$220B capex and 37% AWS growth remain the most recent data points and the clearest capex-payback story of the group. Weight unchanged.

positions.name: Broadcom
positions.note: Fiscal Q3 AI semiconductor revenue hit $16.7B (+221% YoY), beating its own $16.0B guide, and management extended its long-term outlook to ~$115B FY2027 and ~$230B FY2028 — directly resolving last quarter's failure to raise the FY27 number above $100B that had triggered a 12.6% selloff. Named commitments from Google, Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta add real customer specificity.

positions.name: Palantir
positions.note: No new company-specific news this edition; shares remain up over 40% in the past month on an already-stretched multiple following the Aug 4 beat-and-raise. Good business, but the price still assumes flawless execution indefinitely — staying on Watch rather than Core.

positions.name: AMD
positions.note: No new catalyst since the late-August ROCm 10 launch and the reported Cathie Wood trim; Q2 fundamentals (EPS $1.66 vs $0.48) remain strong, but the stock's whipsaw reaction to its own product news keeps this speculative-sized rather than core.

positions.name: Meta
positions.note: No new Meta-specific catalyst this edition; CFO Susan Li's 'highly dynamic' capital planning and the $21B CoreWeave capacity deal already priced in last week's Watch call, and nothing this week resolves the open-ended-spending question.

positions.name: Oracle
positions.note: The Aug 25 downgrade to BBB- and the planned layoffs took effect with the Sept 1 start of fiscal Q2, confirming rather than changing the Avoid call — a widening FY27 free-cash-flow deficit (S&P models ~$42B) funded substantially by equity dilution.

positions.name: UiPath
positions.note: Q2 CY2026 revenue of $410.3M (+13.4% YoY) beat the $397.9M estimate and management raised full-year guidance to ~$1.79B at the midpoint — moving off Avoid to Watch since the agentic-disruption thesis hasn't shown up in the numbers yet, though growth is still a fraction of AI-native peers'.

positions.name: SpaceX
positions.note: Musk said SpaceX will launch its first orbital AI data center using Nvidia technology in Q4 2027, aiming for 'significant scale' by 2028 — interesting long-dated optionality, but xAI's capex burn (more than doubled to $15.8B in Q2) still outruns confirmed new revenue like the Alphabet GPU deal. Staying on Watch.
